title: Loyalist parade in Northern Ireland given go-ahead after ban overturned
description:
Orange Order march along Garvaghy Road could take place for first time in 28 years after injunction dismissed on appeal

A controversial loyalist parade along a nationalist street in Portadown could go ahead for the first time in nearly 30 years, after a ban was overturned late on Saturday night.

The Orange Order parade down the Garvaghy Road will be allowed to go ahead on Sunday morning, following a legal back-and-forth in recent days amid fears the march could unleash fresh sectarian violence.
